plans.pairs: ENH-006 D89 (70% minimal pairs). recipe.json's slot_siblings step adds V = 4 siblings (empty, decoy lookalike, decoy naming_no_value, vetoed masked_value) to every pos carrier; siblings of a held-out genre or generator are dropped (D89: test sets stay real text), so only training carriers get them. With pos share p = 0.32: training rows = C x (1 + pV) = C x 2.28; paired rows = C x p(1 + V) = C x 1.60; paired share = 0.702. Training genres hold 0.815 of the carriers (ten at 0.0815), the two held-out genres 0.185 (0.0925 each), so test_unseen_genre keeps ~3,000 rows while training reaches ~30,000: carriers N = 16200; training carriers 13203 x 2.28 = 30103 rows, 21125 paired (70.2%); held-out genre carriers 2997. Before pairs the plan drew 30,000 carriers; 16,200 is 46% fewer Llama carrier calls (GPU hours scale with carriers; siblings are made by code). Label-flipping pairs: only a pos carrier framed as a disclosure (own_identifier, someones_identifier; 0.55 of carriers) flips; on deployed_truth (D91) its empty and decoy siblings always flip and its masked sibling flips when the form shows the digits (the veto cannot see a rendering), on disclosure the masked sibling keeps the label (D12). Measured shares: backend/tests/integration/behaviour/test_ssn_pilot_elements.py.

second_opinion.note: D66 (operator, 2026-10-25): spend ceiling $5 in total; TypeSafe price measured by the operator: 20,780 tokens over 55 requests cost $0.0008, about $0.0000145 per call. The price field takes six decimals (price_per_call_usd), so the role's price is entered rounded UP to 0.000015 (the conservative side: spend is never under-counted). Both are entered by the operator at 17.1: the classifier role's price in Settings > Endpoints, and CLASSIFIER_SPEND_CEILING_USD (agent-forbidden runtime setting, 'Money: only the operator sets it'); while either is unset every paid run is refused. These values here are the record, not the settings.
second_opinion.estimate: Four label runs (one per compared column), each at most the per-run cap of 2,500 rows: at most 10,000 calls x $0.000015 = $0.15 per full second-opinion pass; the $5 ceiling covers about 33 such passes
